items.title: SASSO, VIA Riyadh
items.note: Doha's award-winning Italian spot just opened its first Saudi branch, with tagliatelle tossed inside a Parmesan wheel.
items.read: KSA Edit reports that SASSO, the Italian restaurant known in Doha for its Parmesan-wheel tagliatelle and Wagyu lasagna, has opened its first Saudi branch at VIA Riyadh in Al Hada. Its Al Hazm branch in Doha won Favourite Italian Fine Dining at the FACT Dining Awards Doha 2022. The Riyadh menu includes Pasta Al Forno, a Wagyu Pinwheel Lasagna, spicy rigatoni with burrata, a wood-fired black truffle pizza and a veal risotto topped with six-hour slow-cooked veal. Prices and online booking haven't been published yet, so tables are booked by contacting the restaurant directly, and booking ahead is advised at weekends.
facts: VIA Riyadh, Makkah Al Mukarramah Rd, Al Hada
items.mapQuery: SASSO VIA Riyadh, Makkah Al Mukarramah Rd, Al Hada

items.title: Shayan, Al Malqa
items.note: New Indian spot with a modern twist: pastry-crusted lamb biryani, mustard prawns and rose falooda.
items.read: This is Riyadh introduced Shayan on 9 November as a new restaurant in Al Malqa serving Indian favourites with a contemporary twist, from rich curries and tandoori dishes to creative starters and desserts. Recommended dishes include a Lamb Curry Biryani baked under a golden sesame pastry crust, Sarson Jhinga char-grilled tiger prawns with yellow mustard, and a Rose Falooda with a kulfi ring, rose milk and basil seeds. The review praises the colourful interior, relaxed atmosphere and generous portions, and suggests ordering several dishes to share.
facts: Anas Bin Malik Rd, Al Malqa
items.mapQuery: Shayan, Anas Bin Malik Rd, Al Malqa

items.title: Le Café NAC pop-up, Diriyah
items.note: London's Belgravia brasserie is doing an outdoor winter residency at Aseel Resort, nightly 6pm to midnight.
items.read: What's On Saudi Arabia reports that Le Café NAC, the French-inspired brasserie on Motcomb Street in London's Belgravia, opened a winter residency at Aseel Resort in Diriyah on Thursday 5 November. The outdoor space has bistro-style chairs, greenery, warm lighting and circular overhead structures. In London the café is known for breakfast burritos, ricotta pancakes, black truffle rigatoni and crushed milk chocolate cookies with soft serve, though the full Diriyah menu hadn't been revealed when the story ran. NAC already has a restaurant at Laysen Valley in Riyadh, and reservations carry a SAR 50 per person booking fee.

items.title: Wonder Garden, Boulevard City
items.note: Riyadh Season's garden-themed family zone returns in a new home in Hittin, opening 18 Nov.
items.read: KSA Edit reports that Wonder Garden, Riyadh Season's garden-themed family zone, is moving to Boulevard City in Hittin and opens on Wednesday 18 November. It is laid out as five areas: the Street Garden with giant screens, food trucks and shops; the Flower Garden with rides and skill games; the atmospheric Mystery Forest; the evening Night Garden; and Strange Creatures in the Imagination Factory, where children build a creature of their own. Ticket prices, hours and the closing date haven't been announced, so check riyadhseason.com before going. Suwaidi Park opens the same day and Al Hisn Maze follows on 19 November.
facts: five themed areas, including a Night Garden

items.title: Riyadh Racing Season, King Abdulaziz Racecourse
items.note: #موسم_سباقات_الرياض is trending in Saudi; races every Fri and Sat, with the Crown Prince Cup on 27 Nov.
items.read: #موسم_سباقات_الرياض and #نادي_سباقات_الخيل are among X's top Saudi trends this morning. According to webook's guide, the 2026–2027 Riyadh Racing Season runs from 16 October 2026 to 17 April 2027 at King Abdulaziz Racecourse, with 50 race days on Fridays and Saturdays and total prize money of SAR 236.3 million. The next big date is the Crown Prince Cup on 27 November, whose prize rose to SAR 1.5 million this season, followed by Kings' Weekend on 18–19 December and the Saudi Cup on 5–6 February 2027. Ticket prices appear on webook.com as each race day opens for booking.

items.title: Powerhouse Parramatta, Sydney
items.note: Sydney's biggest cultural build since the Opera House, opening 7 Nov with mostly free exhibitions.
items.read: The NSW Government announced that Powerhouse Parramatta, Western Sydney's first state cultural institution, would open to the public on Saturday 7 November 2026 on the banks of the Parramatta River. The $915 million project is described as the most significant cultural infrastructure project since the Sydney Opera House, and entry to the museum and most exhibitions is free. The five opening exhibitions show more than 3,000 objects, including Task Eternal with the historic Qantas Avro 504k aircraft, and The Mall, which features Steve Jobs' Levi's 501 jeans and a ballet of warehouse robots by Japanese artist yang02.
facts: free to the museum and most exhibitions

items.title: Jung Kook x Graff “I Wish”
items.note: #JUNGKOOKxGRAFF is trending in Saudi as the holiday film ends with a seven-carat diamond ring reveal.
items.read: Graff's festive campaign “I Wish,” unveiled on 5 November, stars BTS's Jung Kook, the brand's global ambassador, in an all-white jacket and turtleneck layered with pieces from the Lawrence Graff Signature collection, Graff's first unisex jewelry line. In the hero film he says “Graff, I wish for you” and opens a jewelry box to reveal a seven-carat oval diamond ring flanked by heart-shaped shoulder stones. The collection comes in yellow, white and rose gold, with pavé diamond options, and a behind-the-scenes video was released alongside the campaign.

items.title: Google Pixel Tag
items.note: Google's $30 AirTag rival for Android went on sale this week, with a surprise NFC addition.
items.read: TechCrunch reports that the Google Pixel Tag went on sale on 10 November for $29.99, letting Android users find keys, wallets or bags through the Find Hub app with Bluetooth and ultra-wideband precision finding. It is slimmer and more oval than Apple's AirTag, has a physical button and a speaker that reaches about 80 decibels, and relies on a network of over a billion Android devices to locate items that are far away. It runs on a replaceable CR2032 battery rated for up to a year, is IP67 water and dust resistant, and comes in silver and pale green, singly or in a four-pack for $99.99.
facts: Android 9 or newer, via Find Hub
replaceable CR2032, up to one year

items.title: Beni, the jumping robot cameraman
items.note: The follow-you camera robot that went viral with tech YouTubers is now on sale for $799.
items.read: PetaPixel reports that Mondo Robotics' Beni, a rolling robot that follows you and films, went on sale on 10 November after raising over $5 million on Kickstarter and shipping more than 5,000 units to backers in October. It tracks its owner, avoids obstacles, rights itself after a fall and can jump up to 10 inches, which lets it climb stairs; the company says it reaches 17.9 mph. It records 4K at 60fps, 1080p at 120fps or vertical 3K for TikTok and Instagram, with 32GB of storage plus microSD. The Standard kit is $799, and the Explore combo, with three batteries and off-road wheels, is $959.

items.title: Taken: Natalee Holloway
items.note: Netflix's new No. 1 English series, with 12.9M views in its debut week.
items.read: ComingSoon reports that the three-part true-crime docuseries Taken: Natalee Holloway debuted at No. 1 on Netflix's English TV chart for the week of 2 to 8 November 2026, with 12.9 million views. It revisits the May 2005 disappearance of 18-year-old Natalee Holloway during a graduation trip to Aruba, a case that stayed unresolved for years until a major development in 2023. The One About Matthew Perry came second with 4.4 million views, followed by season 3 of Nobody Wants This with 4 million.
facts: The One About Matthew Perry, 4.4M views

items.title: The 10-for-9 sub board and the sarcastic clap
items.note: A football skit where the subbed-off player gives the slowest, most sarcastic applause ever. Over 7M views on one repost alone.
items.read: This one-minute clip, shared by @BenYousef_E with the caption “Who is this guy,” is a staged football comedy skit, not a real match. X's trend summary describes a referee holding up a substitution board with 10 in red and 9 in green while a player in a red shirt gives over-the-top sarcastic applause on his way off, and credits the skit to creator Muhammad Shaif. Troll Football reposted the same video as “My new favourite player” and drew another 3.6 million views. Fans keep calling it the funniest football clip they've seen in ages.

items.title: Little cousins instead of saying hello
items.note: An AI GIF of a baby hippo and an alligator waddling upright, now everyone's reaction for chaotic kids.
items.read: User acce (@accekid) posted a short GIF captioned “What my little cousins do when they see me instead of just saying hello.” According to X's trend summary, the AI-generated clip shows a baby hippo and an alligator walking stiffly on their hind legs down a city street, looking cute but vaguely threatening. People have since reused it for kids demanding snacks, grabbing phones back or swarming relatives at family gatherings, and some are turning it into stickers. It has become one of the most-shared reaction GIFs of the week.

items.title: “I learned to make GIF stickers, I'm going to be unbearable”
items.note: A Spanish post about a TikTok sticker tutorial hit 40M views, and now everyone is pasting GIFs as stickers.
items.read: User @miensha00 posted in Spanish, in all caps, that they had learned to make stickers out of GIFs thanks to a TikTok tutorial and were going to be insufferable, with a GIF attached. The post took off, and a follow-up quote post from @kekatothepink explained that all you have to do is copy a GIF and paste it, adding a 12-second how-to video. That explainer alone pulled about 19.5 million views and nearly 199,000 likes. The combination is a big part of why reaction GIFs like the hippo and alligator are spreading as stickers this week.

items.title: Two rats square up in an alley
items.note: Two rats rear up on their hind legs mid-standoff, and it's the new “don't test me” reaction.
items.read: RIO (@seeka_brian) posted an 11-second clip captioned simply “Wtf” with a laughing emoji. X's trend summary describes two rats standing upright on their hind legs among trash in a grimy alley, mouths open as if about to fight, with the bigger one glaring. Nigerian users started captioning it with everyday standoffs, and it is spreading as a GIF for bold confrontations. Some replies joke that the rats think they're the hippo and alligator.

items.title: The monkey chef who flinches at the steam
items.note: A capuchin shields its face from a smoking wok with a plate, then stirs like a pro.
items.read: User dani (@chukwunonyerem_) posted the GIF with the caption “what is this GIF???” According to X's trend summary, it shows a white-faced capuchin monkey in a rustic kitchen holding up a blue plate to block the steam from a hot wok, then grabbing a ladle and stirring dramatically. Another account, @Trissy001, followed up with the full 21-second video for anyone who wanted it. People are using it as a reaction for shock and disbelief, and one repost called it the funniest GIF they'd ever seen.

items.title: The giant orange cat vs. the yellow truck
items.note: An absurd AI GIF of a huge cat stretching against a truck on a village road has Nigerian X in tears.
items.read: MALEEK 1.0 (@Maleekoyibo) posted the GIF with the caption “This is the funniest thing I have seen today.” X's trend summary describes an oversized orange cat with white paws awkwardly pushing or stretching against a yellow truck on a dusty village road, tail flopping, while people walk past. It is part of a wave of AI-generated cat clips, and replies keep asking who is making all these GIFs. A near-identical share by @Piazon_75 drew a similar audience.

items.title: AI Seinfeld: George and the “Chinese models”
items.note: An AI Seinfeld skit riffs on the Nvidia CEO spy-affair story, the week's biggest meme topic.
items.read: Creator Christian Moss (@MandelDuck) posted a roughly one-minute AI-generated Seinfeld skit captioned “George also enjoys the ‘chinese’ models.” X's trend summary says it puts George Costanza in a plot where a woman posing as a Chinese spy presses him for secret AI models, with Jerry and George reacting from their couch. It riffs on reports about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair and alleged intelligence links, which Know Your Meme says turned into a flood of “honeypot” memes this week. Fans call it AI Seinfeld perfection, while others say the writing doesn't match the show.

items.title: The oven clock says 2:47
items.note: A painfully relatable ADHD time-blindness meme: you have plenty of time, until you don't.
items.read: UltraLittleBirdie (@FluffWingBirdie) shared a roughly one-minute video captioned “So true.” X's trend summary says it uses a kitchen clock stuck at 2:47 to show how people with ADHD glance at the time, decide they have plenty left, then end up rushing as minutes slip away. Replies mixed laughs and relief with personal stories and tips, like stacking calendar alarms or working backward from deadlines.

items.title: Riyadh's mood after the rain
items.note: #امطار_الرياض_الان and #صباح_الاجواء_الحلوه top Saudi trends as rain soaks the capital and nearby schools go remote.
items.read: Rain over Riyadh pushed #امطار_الرياض_الان (Riyadh rain now), #مطر_الليل (night rain) and #صباح_الاجواء_الحلوه (good-weather morning) to the top of X's Saudi trends this morning. This small post from @AFXX990 sums up the vibe with the caption “Riyadh people's mood after the rain” and a laughing emoji, plus attached media. The weather also fed a flurry of school-suspension speculation: a widely viewed post from the account @SahabatAlRiyadh listed governorates such as Al-Majma'ah, Shaqra, Al-Zulfi and Afif switching to remote learning today, and said Riyadh city was already studying remotely. It is a fun local snapshot, not an official announcement.

items.title: “Mister Beast, calm down”
items.note: AI edits make the ever-cheerful MrBeast scream at contestants over tiny mistakes, like dropped blueberries.
items.read: Know Your Meme added an entry on 9 November for MrBeast Chill Out or Crashout edits, AI-assisted clips that make MrBeast appear to explode at people over small mistakes. The earliest known example, from TikToker @ikowels on 28 October, shows him screaming after a contestant drops a container of blueberries, captioned “Mister beast calm down.” Later versions have him yelling at school kids, at a child who fails a challenge, and at someone who admits they don't watch his videos. The joke works because the fake meltdowns are the opposite of his real upbeat persona.
facts: TikTok, then Instagram Reels and X
@texaspja, over 7.8 million views in a week

items.title: Sharq (شرق), Samhania
items.note: Hasawi and Eastern Province cooking in a mudbrick house down a Diriyah alley.
items.read: Sharq serves Hasawi and Eastern Province dishes like Hassawi rice, saleeg and sayyadiyeh. It's tucked into a mudbrick house down an alley in Samhania, Diriyah, which makes it easy to walk past if you're not looking.

items.title: Jadan Cafe
items.note: Small, easy-to-miss Al Arid cafe with V60 coffee, healthy bowls and an owner who knows regulars by name.
items.read: A small neighborhood cafe in Al Arid known for V60 coffee and healthy bowls, with an owner who greets regulars by name. Arab News put a visit at about SAR 20 to 40 a person.

items.title: Haila Coffee
items.note: Hidden inside Souq Al Zal, furnished from the market itself, with Spanish lattes next to kleeja.
items.read: Haila Coffee is tucked into Souq Al Zal, with furniture sourced from the old market. Spanish lattes sit next to kleeja and date-molasses sweets, and reviewers say the entrance is easy to miss. Local posts also point to Haila Tea next door, near Qasr Al Hukm.
facts: Souq Al Zal, near Qasr Al Hukm
items.mapQuery: Haila Coffee Souq Al Zal Riyadh

items.title: Seen
items.note: Al Muruj cafe praised for drip coffee, cortado and especially its karkadeh.
items.read: Seen is an Al Muruj cafe people praise for drip coffee, cortado and especially the karkadeh (hibiscus). The cinnamon rolls and cheesecake get mentions too.

items.title: Floccus
items.note: Open-source bookmark sync across browsers through your own cloud, no Floccus account.
items.read: Floccus keeps bookmarks in sync across Chrome, Firefox, Edge and more using storage you already have, such as Google Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud, Git or S3. There's no Floccus account to create.
facts: Google Drive, Dropbox, Nextcloud, Git, S3

items.title: Super Productivity
items.note: Free open-source task manager with time tracking and focus mode; data stays on your device.
items.read: A free, open-source task manager with built-in time tracking and a focus mode. Your lists stay on the device unless you turn sync on. Its site lists 4.8 from 1,600+ Google Play ratings.
facts: 4.8 from 1,600+ Google Play ratings (per its site)

items.title: Quick Cursor
items.note: Thumb-controlled cursor to reach the top of a big Android screen one-handed.
items.read: Quick Cursor adds a thumb-controlled cursor so you can reach the top of a large Android screen with one hand. It has no ads and no data collection.

items.title: Feeder
items.note: Local-only Android RSS reader that pulls blogs and news into one timeline, no account.
items.read: Feeder is a local-only Android RSS reader that gathers blogs and news into one timeline without an account. Version 2.25.0 was current as of 27 October 2026.
